title: Sass
description: CSS preprocessor adding variables, nesting, and mixins to CSS.

data.text: Sass (Syntactically Awesome Style Sheets) is a CSS preprocessor that extends CSS with features like variables, nesting, mixins, and functions. It compiles to standard CSS that browsers can understand.

data.title: Sass Variables and Nesting
data.content: Define a primary color variable and use nested selectors.

terms.definition: The newer Sass syntax that uses braces and semicolons, like standard CSS.
Reusable blocks of styles that can be included in other selectors.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Sass adds programming features to CSS
Supports variables, nesting, mixins, and inheritance
Compiles to standard CSS for production
data.takeaway: Sass makes CSS more maintainable by adding DRY principles to stylesheets.
